Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 22, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Hajj (the Pilgrimage), because it includes the call to Hajj upon the tongue of Allah's Prophet Ibrahim al-Khalil (the Friend of Allah), peace be upon him, and because it legislates for people the rites of Hajj.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Providing evidence for resurrection, rising again, and the establishment of the Hour through the first creation, and through the sending down of rain upon the dead earth and its revival with vegetation, and that Allah, exalted is He, is true and capable of all of this.

• Mention of the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection and the painful punishment they will meet in the most hideous forms of humiliation and degradation, and mention of the state of the believers and the forms of bliss they will meet in the finest dwellings, the best garments, and adornment.

• Legislation of the rulings related to Hajj and the sacrificial offering (al-hady), and urging the glorification of the sacred rites, and reminding the polytheists of the benefits Allah bestowed upon them through the legislation of Hajj, and of what they must be upon in this rite.

• Legislation of fighting in Islam, and permission to fight the enemies, to repel injustice and aggression, and the glad tidings of Allah's defense of the believers who fight in His cause, and His promise to them of the outcome of victory over those who persecuted them and expelled them from their homes without right.

• Mention of the accounts of the destroyed towns because of their wrongdoing and rebellion, to show the sunnah (way/law) of Allah in punishing the disbelievers, and as consolation to His Messenger (ﷺ) for what he meets of his people's aversion, and as reassurance to the Muslims about the outcome that awaits the patient.

• Affirmation that Allah deserves divinity and oneness, by mentioning the cosmic signs and the divine blessings, and His singularity, exalted is He, in creating and causing death.

[Tafsir]

O mankind, beware of Allah's punishment by complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. What occurs at the establishment of the Hour of terrors and the violent shaking of the earth, whereby all its sides will be split apart, is a tremendous matter, whose magnitude cannot be measured, whose reality cannot be fully reached, and whose manner none knows except the Lord of the worlds.

On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget the infant she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will drop her burden, because of the distress that has befallen them. People's minds will be bewildered, and they will appear like drunkards from the severity of the terror and dread, though they will not be drunk on wine. Rather, the severity of the horror will have robbed them of their reason and their awareness.

And among mankind are some ringleaders of disbelief who dispute and cast doubt on God's power to resurrect, out of ignorance of the reality of this power, and following leaders of misguidance, every devil who rebels against God and His messengers.

God has decreed and ordained concerning this Satan that he misguides everyone who follows him, and does not guide him to the truth; rather, he drives him to the punishment of the blazing Hellfire as a recompense for his following him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 22, verse 5:

﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the resurrection, then (consider that) We created you from dust, then from a drop (of semen), then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, that We may make clear to you. And We cause to remain in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as infants, then (We let you grow) that you may reach your maturity (ashudd). And among you is one who is taken (in death), and among you is one who is returned to the most decrepit age, so that he knows nothing after knowing (much).﴾

Translation of the commentary: We created your father Adam from dust, then his offspring came into being from a nutfah (nuṭfah, a drop), which is the semen that a man ejects into a woman's womb. By God's power it turns into an 'alaqah (ʿalaqah, a clinging clot), which is thick red blood, then into a mudghah (muḍghah, a lump), which is a small piece of flesh about the size of what can be chewed. It is sometimes formed (mukhallaqah), meaning fully formed in creation, ending in the birth of a living child, and at other times unformed, so it falls (as a miscarriage) incomplete. This is so that We may show you the completeness of Our power in turning creation through its stages, and We keep in the wombs whatever We will until the time of birth. The stages are completed by the birth of the fetuses as young children who grow until they reach al-ashudd (the ashudd, full strength), which is the time of youth, strength and full mental maturity. Some children die before that, and some grow until they reach the age of decrepitude and weakness of mind, so this aged person knows nothing of what he used to know before. You see the earth dry and dead, without plants, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs with vegetation, splits open with it, swells and grows due to being watered, and it produces every kind of fine plant that pleases those who look at it.

That which has been mentioned, of the signs of Allah's power set out before it, is a decisive proof that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the Lord who is truly worshipped, the One to whom worship alone is due. He gives life to the dead, and He is capable of everything.
And that the Hour of Resurrection is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that Allah will raise the dead from their graves for their reckoning and recompense.

Among the disbelievers is one who argues about Allah with falsehood, concerning His Oneness, His choice of His Messenger (ﷺ), and His sending down of the Qur'an. That argument is without knowledge, without clarity, and without a Book from Allah containing proof and clear evidence. He turns his neck away in arrogance and turns away from the truth, in order to prevent others from entering the religion of Allah. He will surely meet disgrace in this world, being routed and having his affair exposed, and on the Day of Resurrection We will burn him with the Fire.

Whoever thinks that Allah will not support His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) with victory in this world, by making his religion prevail, and in the Hereafter, by raising his rank and punishing those who denied him, then let him stretch a rope up to the ceiling of his house and hang himself with it. Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 22, verse 25:

Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and deny what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought them, and who prevent others from entering the religion of Allah, and who hinder the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah from the Sacred Mosque, which We have made for all the believers, both the one who dwells in it and the one who comes to it, theirs is a painful, agonizing punishment. And whoever intends in the Sacred Mosque deviation from the truth through wrongdoing, [and] disobeys Allah in it, We will make him taste a painful, agonizing punishment.

And remember, O Prophet, when We showed Ibrahim (ʿalayhi as-salam) the place of the House and prepared it for him, although it had been unknown. We commanded him to build it upon taqwa (God-consciousness) from Allah and upon His tawhid (oneness), and to purify it from disbelief, innovations, and impurities, so that it would be a sacred space for those who circumambulate it and for those who stand in prayer beside it.

Proclaim to the people, O Ibrahim, the obligation of Hajj upon them. They will come to you in their various circumstances, on foot and riding, upon every lean camel (ḍāmir), which is: "the one light of flesh from travel and labor, not from emaciation" (al-khafīf al-laḥm min al-sayr wal-aʿmāl lā min al-huzāl). They will come from every distant path, so that they may witness benefits for themselves: the forgiveness of their sins, the reward for performing their rites and acts of obedience, and their earning through trade, and other things besides. And so that they may mention the name of Allah over the slaughter of the camels, cattle and sheep they offer as acts of drawing near to Him, on specified days: the tenth of Dhu al-Hijjah and the three days after it, in gratitude to Allah for His blessings. They are commanded to eat from these sacrificed animals as a recommended practice, and to feed from them the poor man whose poverty has become severe.

Then let the pilgrims complete what remains of their rites, by ending their state of ihram (ihram: the sacred state entered into for hajj or umrah) and releasing themselves from it, by removing the dirt that has accumulated on their bodies, cutting their nails, and shaving their hair. And let them fulfill what they have made obligatory upon themselves of hajj, umrah, and offerings, and let them circumambulate the Ancient House (al-Bayt al-'Atiq), the old one, which Allah freed from the domination of tyrants, and it is the Ka'bah.

That is what Allah has commanded: the completion of the rites (qada' al-tafath), the fulfilling of vows, and circumambulating the Ancient House. And whoever venerates the sacred rites of Allah (hurumat Allah), among them His rituals (manasikihi), by performing them completely and sincerely for Allah, then that is better for him in this world and the Hereafter. Allah has permitted you to eat cattle (al-an'am), except what He has forbidden to you in what is recited to you in the Qur'an, such as carrion (al-maytah) and other things, so avoid them. In this there is a refutation of what the Arabs used to forbid of some cattle. And keep away from filth (al-qadhara), which is the idols (al-awthan), and from false speech (al-kadhib), which is the fabrication (al-iftira') against Allah.

hanifs devoted to God, sincere in worship of Him alone, turning to Him in devotion and singling Him out for obedience, and turning away from anything else by rejecting shirk. Whoever associates anything with God, then his likeness—in his remoteness from guidance, and in his ruin and fall from the lofty heights of faith to the depths of disbelief, with the devils snatching at him from every side—is like one who has fallen from the sky: either the birds snatch him away and tear his limbs apart, or a violent wind seizes him and hurls him into a far-off place, the utmost remoteness.

That is what Allah has commanded regarding His Tawhid (affirming His oneness) and sincerely devoting worship to Him. Whoever complies with Allah's command and venerates the symbols of the religion, among them the acts of Hajj and its places, and the sacrificial animals slaughtered there, by deeming them good and choosing them to be fat and fine, then this veneration is among the deeds of those whose hearts are characterized by taqwa (God-consciousness, piety) and fear of Allah.

You will derive benefits from these sacrificial animals: wool, milk, riding, and other things that do not harm them, until the time of their slaughter at the Ancient House, which is the entire Sacred Precinct (al-Haram).

And for every community before you We appointed rites of sacrifice, that they should mention the name of Allah over the beasts of livestock He has provided for them. Your God is one God, so submit to Him. And give good tidings, O Prophet, to those who are humble and submissive to their Lord, of the good of this world and the Hereafter.

These humble, submissive people have among their qualities that when God alone is mentioned, they fear His punishment and beware of disobeying Him. When adversity or hardship befalls them, they endure patiently, hoping for reward from God, the Mighty and Majestic. They perform the prayer completely, and in addition they spend from what God has provided them: in what is obligatory upon them, namely zakat and the maintenance of their dependents, and of those whose support is incumbent upon them, and in the way of God, as well as in voluntary charity.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 22, verse 36:

We have made for you the sacrifice of camels and cattle, which are fattened, among the symbols and markers of the religion. It is so that you may draw near to Allah through them. For you, O those who draw near, there is good in their benefits: eating from them, giving charity, reward, and recompense. So say, when slaughtering them: "In the name of Allah." The camels are slaughtered while standing, their legs bound together, three of their legs tied up and the fourth tied, so that when their sides fall to the ground, it becomes permissible to eat them. Let those who draw near eat from them as an act of worship, and let them feed from them the qani' (the poor person who does not ask out of self-restraint) and the mu'tarr (the one who asks because of his need). Thus has Allah subjected the budn (camels fit for sacrifice) to you, so that you may be grateful to Allah for subjecting them to you.

It will not be the flesh of these sacrificial animals, nor their blood, that reaches Allah; rather, what reaches Him is your piety in them, and that the intention behind them be the Face of Allah alone. Likewise He has subjected them to you, O you who draw near (to Allah), so that you may magnify Allah and give thanks to Him for having guided you to the truth, for He is worthy of that. And give good tidings, O Prophet, to the doers of good, those who worship Allah alone and who do good to His creation with every kind of goodness and success.

Indeed, Allah defends the believers against the aggression of the disbelievers and the schemes of the wicked, because He, mighty and majestic, does not love every treacherous betrayer of the trust of his Lord, ungrateful for His blessing.

The Muslims, at the beginning of their affair, were forbidden from fighting the disbelievers and were commanded to be patient with their harm. When the harm inflicted by the polytheists reached its limit, and the Prophet (ﷺ) left Makkah as a emigrant (muhajir) to Madinah, and Islam had become a power, Allah permitted the Muslims to fight, because of the oppression and aggression that had befallen them. Indeed, Allah the Exalted is capable of granting them victory and humbling their enemy.

And We did not send before you, O Messenger, any messenger or prophet except that when he recited what had been sent down to him of the verses, Satan cast into his recitation whisperings and doubts, in order to turn people away from following what he recited and conveyed. Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 22, verse 53:

The Shaytan's casting (of falsehood into the recitation) was not but something that Allah makes a trial for those in whose hearts is doubt and hypocrisy, and for the hard-hearted among the polytheists, upon whom admonition has no effect. Indeed, the wrongdoers among these and those are in severe enmity toward Allah and His Messenger, and in opposition to the truth, far from what is correct.

And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth sent down from your Lord, so they believe in it and their hearts humbly submit to it. Indeed, Allah guides those who believe to the straight path of truth, which is Islam, rescuing them by it from misguidance.

Wait, that is not a faithful rendering of the passage. Here is the accurate translation:

Those who have knowledge, and who distinguish through their knowledge between truth and falsehood, should know that the Noble Qur'an is the truth sent down from Allah to you, O Messenger. There is no doubt in it, and no way for Satan to reach it, so that their faith increases through it and their hearts submit to it. Indeed, Allah guides those who believe in Him and in His Messenger to the clear path of truth, which is Islam, by which He rescues them from misguidance.

And the disbelievers who deny will not cease to be in doubt about what you have brought them of the Qur'an, until the Hour comes upon them suddenly while they are still in their denial, or there comes upon them the punishment of a day in which there is no good for them, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

The sovereignty and dominion on this Day belong to Allah alone, and He, glory be to Him, judges between the believers and the disbelievers. As for those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did righteous deeds, they will have everlasting bliss in the Gardens. And as for those who denied the oneness of Allah, denied His Messenger, and rejected the verses of the Qur'an, they will have a punishment that disgraces and humiliates them in Hellfire.

As for those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did righteous deeds, they will have everlasting bliss in the Gardens. And as for those who denied the oneness of Allah, denied His Messenger, and rejected the verses of the Qur'an, they will have a punishment that disgraces and humiliates them in Hellfire.

Those who emigrated from their homes seeking the pleasure of Allah and supporting His religion, whether they were killed while striving against the disbelievers or died without fighting, Allah will surely provide for them with Paradise and its bounties, which never end and never cease. Indeed, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is the best of those who provide sustenance.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 22, verse 59:

Allah will certainly admit them to an admission that they will love, which is Paradise. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of those who go out in His cause, and of those who go out seeking worldly gain. He is Forbearing toward those who disobey Him, so He does not hasten to punish them.

This is the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 22, verse 60:

That is the matter: We have related to you how the emigrants will be admitted into Paradise. And whoever has been transgressed against and wronged, it has been permitted for him to respond to the aggressor with the same as what he did to him, and there is no blame upon him. Then if the aggressor returns to harming him and transgresses, God will surely help the wronged one who was transgressed against, since it is not permissible for him to be transgressed against on account of his taking redress for himself. Indeed, God is Most Pardoning, Oft-Forgiving: He pardons the sinners and does not hasten to punish them, and He forgives their sins.

That is the One who has prescribed for you those just rulings; He is the Truth, and He is capable of whatever He wills. From His power is that He makes the night enter into the day, so that what is lost from the hours of the night is added to the hours of the day, and makes the day enter into the night, so that what is lost from the hours of the day is added to the hours of the night. And Allah is All-Hearing of every sound, All-Seeing of every deed; nothing is hidden from Him.

That is because Allah is the true God, and worship is due to none but Him. And what the polytheists worship besides Him, of idols and rivals, is falsehood, which neither benefits nor harms. And Allah is the Most High over His creation in His essence, His power, and His dominion, exalted above likenesses and equals, great in His essence, His names, and His attributes. So He is greater than everything.

Have you not seen, O Messenger, that Allah sends down water from the sky, and so the earth becomes green with the plants that grow in it? Indeed, Allah is Subtle (Latif) with His servants in bringing forth vegetation from the earth through that water, and Acquainted (Khabir) with their interests.

God, glorified and exalted is He, owns whatever is in the heavens and the earth, by creation, by possession, and by worship; all of it is in need of His management and bounty. Indeed, God is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani) who has no need of anything, the Praiseworthy in every state.

Have you not seen that Allah has made subservient to you whatever is on the earth: the animals, the beasts, the crops, the fruits, and the inanimate things, for your riding and your sustenance, and for all your benefits; just as He has made subservient to you the ships that run upon the sea by His power and command, carrying you together with your goods to whatever lands and places you wish. And it is He who holds up the sky, preserving it so that it does not fall upon the earth and destroy those on it, except by His permission, glorified is He? Indeed Allah is Most Merciful to people with a vast mercy, in their present life and in their life to come. And among His mercy towards them is what He has subjected to them of these things and others, as a bounty from Him upon them.

He is Allah, exalted is He, who gave you life by bringing you into existence from non-existence, then causes you to die when your lifespans come to an end, then will give you life again through resurrection to call you to account for your deeds. Indeed, man is truly ungrateful and denying of the clear signs that point to Allah's power and His oneness.

For every community We have appointed rites of worship which they observe. So let them not dispute with you over the matter, O Messenger, and call (them) to the worship of your Lord. Indeed, you are upon a straight guidance.

Note: the commentary text above is the translation of the verse. The passage you provided is the explanatory text of the Muyassar tafsir for Surah al-Hajj 22:67, which reads:

For every community of the earlier nations We prescribed a law and a form of worship which We commanded them to follow, and they are acting upon it. So let not the polytheists of Quraysh dispute with you, O Messenger, concerning your law, nor concerning what Allah has commanded you regarding the rites of Hajj and all kinds of worship. Call to the Oneness of your Lord, to sincerity in worshipping Him alone, and to following His command. Indeed, you are upon a straight religion, with no crookedness in it.

And if they persist in disputing with you falsely about what you call them to, then do not dispute with them; rather, say to them: "Allah knows best what you do of disbelief and denial," for they are stubborn and obstinate.

God, exalted is He, will judge between the Muslims and the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection concerning their disagreement in religion. And in this verse there is a fine etiquette in responding to those who argue out of obstinacy and arrogance.

Did you not know, O Messenger, that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth with complete knowledge, which He has recorded in the Preserved Tablet? Indeed, that knowledge is easy for Allah, who is not overcome by anything.

The Quraysh disbelievers insist on associating partners with Allah even though the falsehood of what they follow is evident. They worship deities for which no proof was ever sent down in any of the Books of Allah showing that they are fit to be worshipped. They have no knowledge of what they have invented and fabricated against Allah; rather, it is merely a matter that they followed their forefathers in, without any evidence. So when the time of reckoning comes in the Hereafter, the polytheists will have no helper to support them or to ward off the punishment from them.

When the clear verses of the Qur'an are recited to these polytheists, you can see the aversion plainly on their faces. They nearly lash out at the believers who call them to God Most High and recite His verses to them. Say to them, O Messenger: "Shall I inform you of something more hateful to you than hearing the truth and seeing those who call to it? It is the Fire, which God has prepared for the disbelievers in the Hereafter, and wretched is the place to which they will go."

O mankind, a parable is set forth, so listen to it and reflect upon it: Indeed, the idols and rivals that you worship besides Allah could not, even if they all gathered together, create a single fly. So how could they create something greater? And if the fly snatches anything away from them, they could not even recover it from it. Is there, then, any weaker than this? Both are weak together: the seeker, which is the one worshipped besides Allah, is too weak to rescue what the fly has taken from it, and the sought, which is the fly, is weak. So how can these idols and rivals be taken as gods, when they are in such humiliation?
These polytheists did not venerate God with the veneration He deserves, for they made partners with Him, while He is the Strong who created everything, the Mighty who cannot be overpowered.

Allah, glory be to Him, chooses messengers from among the angels to bring His revelation to His prophets, and He chooses messengers from among mankind to convey His messages to creation. Indeed Allah is All-Hearing of the words of His servants, All-Seeing of all things, and of whoever He chooses for the message from among His creation. He, glory be to Him, knows what is before His angels and His messengers before He created them, and He knows what will be after their passing. And to Allah alone all matters are returned.

Allah, glory be to Him, chooses messengers from among the angels to bring His revelation to His prophets, and He chooses messengers from among mankind to convey His messages to creation. Indeed Allah is All-Hearing of the words of His servants, All-Seeing of all things, and of whoever He chooses for the message from among His creation. He, glory be to Him, knows what is before His angels and His messengers before He created them, and He knows what will be after their passing. And to Allah alone all matters are returned.

O you who have believed, bow and prostrate yourselves in your prayer, worship your Lord alone with no partner, and do good deeds, that you may succeed. And strive against yourselves, and stand in complete devotion to the command of Allah, and call people to His path, and strive with your wealth, your tongues and yourselves, sincere in intention to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, submitting your hearts and limbs to Him. He has chosen you to bear this religion, and He has favoured you by making your law easy, with no constriction or hardship in its obligations and rulings, unlike what was upon some nations before you. This lenient creed is the creed of your father Ibrahim (Abraham). Allah named you "the Muslims" previously in the earlier revealed scriptures and in this Qur'an, and He has singled you out with this choosing, so that the seal of the messengers, Muhammad (ﷺ), may be a witness over you that he conveyed the message of his Lord to you, and that you may be witnesses over the nations that their messengers conveyed to them what Allah has informed you of in His Book. So it is incumbent upon you to recognise the worth of this blessing, so that you may be thankful for it, and to safeguard the landmarks of the religion of Allah by performing the prayer with its pillars and conditions and paying the obligatory zakat, and to turn to Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and rely upon Him. For He is the best of protectors for whoever takes Him as protector, and the best of helpers for whoever seeks His help.
